## Mission result

Create one local Git repository, make one commit, and show the commit in the history. No GitHub account or Wi-Fi is required.

## Before you start

Use a teacher-approved folder. Do not include passwords, tokens, student numbers, private photographs, or files belonging to another student.

## Complete the mission

Open a terminal in your project folder.

```bash
git init
git status
```

Create or edit one small file such as `README.md` or `index.qmd`. Then run:

```bash
git status
git add README.md
git diff --staged
git commit -m "Start my course website"
git log --oneline
```

If you edited `index.qmd`, replace `README.md` with `index.qmd` in the `git add` command.

::: {.callout-tip title="If Git asks who you are"}
Use the classroom identity supplied by the teacher. Configure it for this repository only:

```bash
git config user.name "Student Name or Initials"
git config user.email "student@localhost"
```

Then run the commit command again.
:::

## Success check

You are finished when:

1. `git status` says there is nothing to commit;
2. `git log --oneline` shows your commit;
3. you can explain that saving changes a file while committing records a named checkpoint.

## Submit

Submit one screenshot containing the project folder name and `git log --oneline`. Do not submit the entire computer home folder.
